posts.name: Gaurav
posts.cooked:
Due to subpar health during past week I wasn’t able to submit python GrPAs for week 3, I tried but it was repeatedly showing something went wrong and I couldn’t come to make changes on time.

Will I be eligible to write oppe 1?

According to grading policy it says you have to submit all week GrPA and score >=40/100, isn’t that which isn’t the case for any other subject so far ,even if you miss one/two/multiple week’s graded assignments, you can still write both quizzes it only affects your final score in the range of 1-10 GPA marks depending on the number of weeks you missed.

OLD PYTHON GRADING POLICY = T = 0.1 GAA1 (objective) + 0.1GAA2 (programming) + 0.1Qz1+ 0.4F+ 0.25 max(PE1, PE2) + 0.15 min(PE1, PE2) — capped to 100

If ineligiblity were to exist in first place for OPPE, it could be justified in old python grading policy, since Max possible T was 110. Missing one oppe still leaves you at max T (110 - 15) = 95/100. Student can still aim for S grade ideally, if not, A is still excellent score practically.

NEW PYTHON GRADING POLICY = T = 0.15Qz1+ 0.4F+ 0.25 max(PE1, PE2) + 0.2 min(PE1, PE2)

In new grading policy max T is already 100 and missing one oppe can bring your max T to (100 - 20) = 80/100. You’re direct pushed into ideally either B grade or practically C grade.

Since OPPE has very high weightage in python course, more than quiz 1 and there isn’t even a quiz 2. I want to request you to take a second look with some leniency on the strict python oppe eligibility, please. A small amount of leniency would ensure that dedicated students aren’t disproportionately penalized for minor gaps in weekly submissions.

A single bad week can tank the entire semester’s grade from S/A to B/C. Currently GrPA eligibility for oppe is “all or nothing”, I request you to add some buffer for one bad week in any unforeseen event. This creates extreme anxiety among students. Python is way more punitive compared to any foundation course with a single bad week. And it’s also new course for students with no coding background, who are already finding it a little tricky to handle.

all_posts.cooked:
Where is your logic coming from? What’s the point of calculating 95/115 percentage? 10% of quiz questions in End term? Bonus? What even? Don’t add noise to the discussion.

95/115 ≈ 85%? You’re getting grades out of 100 only, max possible T of 110/100 was a BUFFER for missed oppe since oppe was always a high stake game due to strict eligibility, every week of the term counts to even get eligible to sit in exam, how your exam goes is out of question if you miss a single week, 3 weeks grind, one week sick or whatever emergency your score is tanked in new policy, which wasn’t the case earlier, that’s the reason concept of buffer exists in high stake exams.

And as far as I have heard from people bonus is maxed at 2 now and 1 for sct approval.

Don’t even bring up bonus in this. if it existed before (110+3-15)/100 = 98/100.
It might still exist, Def won’t increase, be it 3 or 5.
I’m taking 2 + 1 = 3 in both cases (100+3-20)/100 = 83/100, and there is no specified criteria for giving out bonus, so don’t even add it in either cases.

And why are you even bringing up missing on quiz? Quiz has nothing to do with a missed week assignment. No one intentionally misses quiz, missed quiz had even lesser effect on final grade in old policy.

Since you have brought it up, now here are all possible cases -

A. Old policy

(a) missed one week GrPA(-1), hence oppe ineligible (-15)
T = (110 - 15-1)/100 = 94/100
Final possible grade = ideally S / practically A

(b) missed quiz (-10)
T = (110-10)/100 = 100/100
Final possible grade = S

(c) missed both, quiz (-10) and one week GrPA(-1), ineligible for oppe (-15)
T = (110 - 10 - 15 - 1)/ 100 = 84/ 100
Final possible grade = ideally A/ practically B
(least effort pathway in old policy)

B. New policy

(a) missed one week GrPA, hence oppe ineligible (-20)
T = (100 - 20)/100 =80/100
Final possible grade = B

(b) missed quiz only (-15)
T = (100 - 15) / 100 =85/100
Final possible grade = ideally A / practically B

(c) missed both, quiz (-15) and one week GrPA, ineligible for oppe (-20)
T = (100 - 20 - 15)/ 100 = 65/ 100
Final possible grade = ideally C / practically D

See the difference for yourself, while old policy’s S/A advocates for integrity, and new policy B/C advocates for perfection, course grade tanked. same effort leads to a difference of two levels in final grade due to new changes.

It’s not hard to miss one week GrPA or quiz day, IITM already knows it, that’s why they had 2 formulae in other foundation courses max of (0.2Qz1 + 0.3Qz2 + 0.4F / 0.2Qz1/Qz2 + 0.6 F), same logic Buffer.

And I’m not even saying new policy is bad or whatever, it’s absolutely fine, but since buffer for missing oppe is gone, so should the strictness of eligibility, there should be at least (N-1) one week missed relaxation, 3 out 4 weeks.

And at this point it doesn’t matter, whatever the policy or eligibility criteria is, It is what it is. thanks for your understanding, it seems either you’re done with python or you haven’t got sick in any of the weeks so far, good luck, there is no point in explaining it anymore. Also if you see something disproportionate, you raise the concern, not dismiss it by saying focus on quiz 1 and oppe 2, it goes without saying. Think it through before trying to advocate it wrongly. Now don’t come up with saying they’re doing it in all courses, what is not right Is not right.
90% in quiz 1, 80% in Oppe 2, 85% in end term, all great scores.
what do you end up with?
(90 *0.15)+(80*0.25)+(85*0.4) = 67.5% = C Grade.

grading policy isn’t law of nature, it’s man made policy and I’m hoping that whoever made it is open to suggestions. Missing one week doesn’t mean you didn’t learn, it just means life happened. A 20% penalty by making you ineligible to sit in exam for a missed week assessment is considered extreme.

And the most popular post in ‘programming in python’ category says the grades have been plummeting in past terms and if this is the new policy, you’ll see an even greater fall in python grades, just wait for the new analysis, it absolutely works against students, we are humans and unforseen things do happen in life.

No further comments from my side.
